[[File: Wes Anderson at the 2018 Berlin Film Festival.jpg|thumb|upright|Anderson at the [[2018 Berlin Film Festival]]]]
[[Wes Anderson]] is an American filmmaker known for feature films, commercials, and short films.

Anderson directed the short film ''Bottle Rocket'' which was later adapted into his feature length directorial debut film ''[[Bottle Rocket]]'' (1996). He later directed his sophomore film ''[[Rushmore (film)|Rushmore]]'' (1998), which established himself as an independent film auteur. He often collaborated with the brothers [[Luke Wilson]] and [[Owen Wilson]] during that time and founded his production company American Empirical Pictures. He further established his unique style with ''[[The Royal Tenenbaums]]'' (2001), ''[[The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou]]'' (2004), ''[[The Darjeeling Limited]]'' (2007), and his first [[stop-motion]] film, ''[[Fantastic Mr. Fox (film)|Fantastic Mr. Fox]]'' (2009), ''[[Moonrise Kingdom]]'' (2012), and ''[[The Grand Budapest Hotel]]'' (2014)

His later works include his second stop-motion film, ''[[Isle of Dogs (film)|Isle of Dogs]]'' (2018), the anthology comedy ''[[The French Dispatch]]'' (2021), the science fiction dramedy ''[[Asteroid City]]'' (2023) and the espionage caper comedy ''[[The Phoenician Scheme]]'' (2025). Anderson won the [[Academy Award for Best Live Action Short Film]] for ''[[The Wonderful Story of Henry Sugar (film)|The Wonderful Story of Henry Sugar]]'' (2023).

==Frequent collaborators==
Anderson's films feature many recurring actors, including the Wilson brothers ([[Owen Wilson|Owen]], [[Luke Wilson|Luke]], and [[Andrew Wilson (actor)|Andrew]]), [[Bill Murray]], [[Jason Schwartzman]], [[Anjelica Huston]], [[Willem Dafoe]], [[Jeff Goldblum]], [[Edward Norton]], [[Adrien Brody]], [[Bob Balaban]], and [[Tilda Swinton]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gottlieb |first=Meryl |date=March 21, 2018 |title=The actors who have appeared in the most Wes Anderson films — from Bill Murray to Owen Wilson |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/actors-in-most-wes-anderson-movies-bill-murray-owen-wilson-2018-3 |access-date=August 4, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Munton |first=Rebecca |date=May 20, 2021 |title=10 Recurring Wes Anderson Collaborators Also In The French Dispatch |url=https://screenrant.com/french-dispatch-recurring-wes-anderson-collaborators/ |access-date=August 4, 2021}}</ref> [[Robert Yeoman]] has served as director of photography for all of Anderson's live-action films, while [[Mark Mothersbaugh]] composed Anderson's first four films, with [[Alexandre Desplat]] composing all since ''Fantastic Mr. Fox.''<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 1, 2018 |title=Directors Trademarks: Wes Anderson |url=https://www.cinelinx.com/movie-news/movie-stuff/directors-trademarks-wes-anderson/ |access-date=August 7, 2021 |website=Cinelinx |archive-date=October 28, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211028150530/https://www.cinelinx.com/movie-news/movie-stuff/directors-trademarks-wes-anderson/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> [[Randall Poster]] has served as music supervisor for all of Anderson's films since ''Rushmore.'' His films have often been financed by [[Steven Rales]] through his production company [[Indian Paintbrush (company)|Indian Paintbrush]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Eisler |first1=Kim |date=December 11, 2007 |title=What's a DC Billionaire Doing Aboard The Darjeeling Limited? |url=https://washingtonian.com/2007/12/11/whats-a-dc-billionaire-doing-aboard-the-darjeeling-limited/|access-date=April 2, 2023 |website=Washingtonian.com}}</ref>
